headword: {終身雇用制|しゅうしんこようせい}
reading: しゅうしんこようせい

definitions.explanation: A Japanese employment practice in which workers are hired straight out of school and remain with one company until retirement.

examples.japanese: {終身雇用制|しゅうしんこようせい}は{日本|にほん}の{伝統的|でんとうてき}な{働|はたら}き{方|かた}だ。
examples.english: The lifetime employment system is a traditional Japanese way of working.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{終身雇用制|しゅうしんこようせい}が{崩|くず}れつつあると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Recently it is said that the lifetime employment system is breaking down.

examples.japanese: {大企業|だいきぎょう}では{終身雇用制|しゅうしんこようせい}がまだ{根強|ねづよ}く{残|のこ}っているが、{若|わか}い{世代|せだい}の{間|あいだ}では{転職|てんしょく}が{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}になってきた。
examples.english: In large corporations, the lifetime employment system still remains deeply rooted, but among the younger generation, changing jobs has become commonplace.

notes:
One of the three pillars of traditional Japanese corporate culture, along with {年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ} (seniority-based promotion) and {企業別組合|きぎょうべつくみあい} (company-based unions). Under this system, employees join a company after graduating and stay until {定年|ていねん} (mandatory retirement age), in exchange for job security and gradually increasing pay.

This practice became widespread during Japan's postwar economic boom but has been declining since the 1990s as globalization, economic stagnation, and changing attitudes have made job-hopping more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {終身雇用制|しゅうしんこようせい}が{崩|くず}れる: the lifetime employment system collapses
- {終身雇用制|しゅうしんこようせい}を{維持|いじ}する: to maintain lifetime employment
- {終身雇用制|しゅうしんこようせい}の{見直|みなお}し: review of lifetime employment

RELATED WORDS:
- {終身雇用|しゅうしんこよう}: lifetime employment (without the {制|せい} suffix)
- {年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ}: seniority-based system
- {転職|てんしょく}: changing jobs
- {定年|ていねん}: mandatory retirement age
